findings.summary: The script-block rule says every pwsh script block is refused, but its trigger list is not exhaustive.
findings.evidence: docs/briefs/B20261126-1008-b42-i162-fence-reads-pwsh.loop-brief.md:149-156 defines a PowerShell `{ ... }` script block as refused only at start or after a command name, parameter, `&`, `.`, or `|`. The summary at lines 49-51 says a script block is refused without that positional limit; PowerShell also admits a script-block expression in other positions, for example after `,` or `=`. A planner that implements the listed trigger positions literally can allow a form the brief says is refused.
findings.fix: Require every unquoted `{ ... }` that opens a PowerShell script block to be refused, explicitly including positions after punctuation and assignment; alternatively, name every remaining script-block position as out of scope and reconcile the W2 summary. Keep the literal W2 denial reason.

findings.summary: Invalid `$env:` statements point to today's unspecified refusal instead of pinning the observable reason.
findings.evidence: docs/briefs/B20261126-1008-b42-i162-fence-reads-pwsh.loop-brief.md:168-172 says every other `$env:` statement "keeps today's refusal". The worked example at line 240 pins only the no-space `$env:GOOS=$x` token; a spaced form begins with a different token and currently reports `command word $env:GOOS starts with $ and cannot be judged` from internal/fence/judge.go:331-333. A gate comparing invalid forms has no single literal contract value.
findings.fix: Pin the reason for each invalid class (including spaced assignment and forms with invalid names or values). For example, state that any refused `$env:` form keeps the exact `<first word>` shown by `command word <word> starts with $ and cannot be judged`, and include representative spaced and otherwise-invalid examples in the worked example.

decisions: Keep parity with sh: the fence remains advisory, and PowerShell file cmdlets and script-file execution stay outside its path-writing judgment.
Judge pwsh/powershell -Command and cmd /c or /k through rather than refusing those wrappers outright.
Refuse dynamic PowerShell execution commands and script blocks rather than implementing a PowerShell parser.
Read only the parenthesized pipeline property form and literal $env assignment; keep other PowerShell syntax fail-closed.
Apply W2-W4 only to a powershell tool call and to a W1-wrapped PowerShell string; a direct bash call remains POSIX.
Update the fence guide, audit and command help, but not skills; the denial guidance is the agent-facing steering.
